info.title: VPNDetection API
info.description:
The VPNDetection API: classify any IP address, and download the databases
behind the answers.

Lookups need no API key: Unlimited, the free plan, answers any address with
no daily or monthly cap, with a key or without one. Every paid plan answers
every field, and a free account tries them. Unlimited's answers may be used
commercially, but not redistributed or used in a competing service
(https://vpndetection.io/terms#no-key).

See https://docs.vpndetection.io for guides and https://github.com/vpndetection-io
for the official client libraries.

get.description:
Answers what is known about a single IPv4 or IPv6 address. Which fields
come back is decided by the presented key; with no key, on Unlimited,
the free plan, the answer is `ip`, `is_vpn`, the Tor and relay members,
`is_anycast`, `hostname`, `location` and `asn`.

parameters.description: The IPv4 or IPv6 address to classify.

get.description:
Answers what is known about the address this request came from, which is
the same answer `GET /{ip}` gives for that address: the presented key
decides which fields come back, and the request counts against the same
limits.

The address is the one our edge observed, so a request through a proxy
or a VPN reports the exit it left through rather than the machine that
made it. That is usually the point of asking.

200.description:
The classification of your own address. Present fields are those
your plan includes; see the tier table in the API description.

401.description: The presented API key is unknown, revoked, or expired.

post.description:
Answers up to 1000 addresses in one call. Each distinct string in `ips`
is one lookup: it costs exactly what `GET /{ip}` costs for that address
and comes back with exactly the fields that call would carry for your
plan. Exact duplicates collapse to one entry and one lookup.

Both maps in the answer are keyed by the string you sent, so nothing has
to be lined up by position; the `ip` inside each result is the
normalized form. An address that could not be answered sits in `errors`
with the status and message the single lookup would have given, and
never disturbs the others: a string that is not an address is a `400`
there. An overage cap reached part way through answers the remaining
entries with Unlimited's fields and `cap_reached` `true`, in `results`.

The call itself fails only for the reasons below, and a `429` on the
call always carries `Retry-After`: the batch is admitted or refused
whole by the rate limit, never per entry.

A batch needs a paid plan: without a key the call is refused with `401`,
and with a key on the free plan with `402`, unless it names one address,
which is answered as `GET /{ip}` would answer it, under the same rate
limit. Unlimited looks up one address at a time.

200.description:
One entry per distinct input string, in `results` or in `errors`.
Present fields within a result are those your plan includes; see the
tier table in the API description.

value.error: body must be a JSON object whose ips member is an array of strings
ips must hold between 1 and 1000 addresses

presented is unknown, revoked, or expired.

get.description:
Every database this organization can see, licensed or not. `standing`
says where its license stands: `licensed`, `expired`, or `unlicensed`
for one never bought.
Redirects (`302`) to a time-limited link to the database file. The link only has to be valid when the download starts, so a long one isn't cut off when it expires.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description:
Not every database is built in every format. The `_provider`
catalogs are keyed by provider ID rather than by IP range, so no
MMDB exists for them.

parameters.name: build
parameters.description:
One build of the database, by the name a `database.updated` webhook
gives it, so the file is the one whose `sha256` the webhook carries.
Without it, the build that is live.

302.description: Follow the Location header to object storage

400.description: The database is not built in the requested format (`INVALID_FORMAT`), or `build` is not a build's name (`INVALID_BUILD`)

403.description: Your organization holds no license for this database, or its term has ended (`NOT_LICENSED`); or the key was sent over plain HTTP (`KEY_OVER_HTTP`), so use `https://`

410.description: The build named in `build` is no longer kept (`BUILD_GONE`); builds are kept 7 days. Download without `build` for the live one

503.description: Licensed, but today's copy has not been published yet

get.description:
Poll this to decide whether today's build is worth fetching: it carries
`updated` and `entries` without downloading anything.

No `format` parameter - one document describes every format the database
is built in. Needs no license: it answers for every database `list`
returns, whatever its `standing`.
Checksums for one published file, so a download can be verified after it lands.

400.description: The database is not built in the requested format

403.description: Your organization holds no license for this database, or its term has ended (`NOT_LICENSED`); or the key was sent over plain HTTP (`KEY_OVER_HTTP`), so use `https://`

get.description: Recent download attempts for this organization, newest first. Refusals are listed too, so a failed transfer can be accounted for.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many attempts to return. Clamped to 1 through 200.

get.description:
Answers what the presented key is, what plan is behind it, and what has
been spent against that plan's allowance in the current window.

paid.summary: A key on a paid plan, uncapped

free.summary: A key of an organization on the free plan, Unlimited: its usage is its trial, the lookups answered with every field, out of the quota the trial has. Nothing stops it past them, its lookups answering with Unlimited's fields, so there is no hard limit.

401.description: No key was presented, or it is unknown, revoked or expired.

value.error: an API key is required
invalid API key
API key revoked
API key expired

403.description:
The key restricts which source addresses may use it, and this
request did not come from one of them; or the key was sent over
plain HTTP, which is refused whatever the key.

value.error: source address not allowed for this API key
API key sent over plain HTTP; use https://

503.description:
The usage counters could not be read. Reported rather than guessed
at: the whole answer is the number, and a confident zero would read
as "you have used nothing".

get.description:
The identity behind this credential: what it is, the organization it is
scoped to, and the scopes it currently holds.

`user` is present for an OAuth token and absent for an API key, which
has an organization but no person behind it. `credential.kind` says
which you are holding, so a client can branch without guessing from a
missing field.

`scopes` is what the credential may do now, so a client can check
before it calls.

Needs the `account.read` scope.

The organization this credential is scoped to.

A credential belongs to one organization, so this takes no ID.

Needs the `org.read` scope.

The members of the organization this credential is scoped to.

Read-only. Members are invited by email from the console.

Needs the `org.read` scope.

Each key's metadata. A list never carries a secret, here or in the
console: `reveal` reads one.

`retrievable` says whether the secret could still be read back at all.
A key issued before this product stored secrets recoverably was never
kept, so `reveal` will refuse it permanently; rotating produces one
that can be read.

Needs the `apikeys.read` scope.

post.description:
Creates a key and returns its secret.

Store the secret now. Reading it back later takes `reveal` and the
`apikeys.reveal` scope.

Needs the `apikeys.manage` scope.

200.description: The new key, including its secret.

post.description:
Replaces the secret behind a key, keeping its ID, name and settings.
The previous secret stops working immediately. The new secret comes
back in the answer, so this needs `apikeys.reveal` as well as
`apikeys.manage`.

200.description: The key, with its new secret.

post.description:
Stops the key working. Revocation is soft: the key stays listed with a
`revoked_at`, because the organization still owns whatever it did while
it was alive.

Needs the `apikeys.manage` scope.

Returns an existing key's secret.

It needs the `apikeys.reveal` scope, which `apikeys.manage` doesn't
include.

Refused with `NOT_RETRIEVABLE` for a key issued before we kept secrets.
Rotate that key instead.

Needs the `apikeys.reveal` scope.

404.description:
No such key in this organization, or its secret was never stored
recoverably (`NOT_RETRIEVABLE`).

get.description:
RFC 8414 authorization server metadata: the endpoints, the grant types
and the scopes this server supports.

Read this rather than hardcoding endpoints. It is also served at
`/.well-known/openid-configuration`, identically, because several
clients probe that path first.

post.description:
Starts the device flow. Show the `user_code` to the person and send them
to `verification_uri`; `verification_uri_complete` has the code already
embedded, which is what to open if you can open a browser at all.

Then poll `/oauth/token`, no faster than `interval` seconds.

400.description:
`invalid_request`, `unauthorized_client` when the client may not use
the device flow, or `slow_down` when this address has started too
many authorizations.

post.description:
RFC 7591 dynamic client registration, for a client that cannot use a
Client ID Metadata Document. Post your client's metadata as JSON, then
use the `client_id` in the answer at `/oauth/authorize` and
`/oauth/token`. Nothing is kept until a person approves your client, so
registering again costs nothing and leaves nothing to clean up.

Each redirect URI must be https on a public host name, or http on a
loopback address (`127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`, `localhost`), which then
matches on any port. A custom URI scheme is refused: use a loopback
redirect instead. So is a host on one of our own domains.

`client_name` is shown to the person as your client's own claim, with
where its redirect goes beside it. A name that renders blank, or mixes
Latin letters with Cyrillic or Greek ones, is shown as an unnamed
application.

The client is public whatever you ask for: `token_endpoint_auth_method`
comes back `none`, there is no client secret, and every authorization
proves itself with PKCE. It may be granted `apikeys.use` at most.

400.description:
`invalid_redirect_uri` names the redirect URI refused and why, and
`invalid_client_metadata` anything else, such as a client that
does not use the authorization code flow. `slow_down` means this
address registered too many clients in the last minute.

get.description:
The browser entry point for the authorization-code flow. This is a
redirect target, not something to call from code.

Any client may sign in without registering first by using a Client ID
Metadata Document: make `client_id` an https URL that serves your
client's metadata as JSON, naming that same URL as its `client_id`,
with `token_endpoint_auth_method` `none` and your `redirect_uris`. An
https redirect URI must be on the same origin as the `client_id`; a
loopback one (`http://127.0.0.1`, `http://[::1]`, `http://localhost`)
matches on any port. Such a client is granted `apikeys.use` at most. A
client registered at `/oauth/register` uses the `client_id` it was
given and one of the `redirect_uris` it registered.

An unknown `client_id` or an unregistered `redirect_uri` is shown to the
person and never redirected, because sending an error to an address we
have not verified belongs to you is how an open redirector works. Any
other error in the request is shown to the person too: anyone can make a
client, so its `redirect_uri` is verified only as its own (RFC 9700
section 4.11.2). Only the person's answer comes back to your
`redirect_uri`: a `code`, or `error` `access_denied`, each with your
`state` and `iss`.

parameters.name: code_challenge_method
parameters.description: S256, named explicitly. `plain`, or no method at all, is refused rather than downgraded.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Returned unchanged. Use it to bind the response to your request.

parameters.name: resource
parameters.description:
RFC 8707. What the token is FOR, so it cannot be replayed elsewhere:
this brand's MCP server, the only resource it issues tokens for.
Anything else answers `invalid_target`. A client that names none is
given that server.

302.description: A redirect to the consent screen.

400.description: Shown to the person. No error in the request is sent to your redirect_uri.

429.description: Shown to the user. Too many authorizations from one address.

post.description:
Issues tokens for three grant types: a device code, an authorization
code and a refresh token.

`urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code` polls a device
authorization. Until the person approves it answers
`authorization_pending`; poll faster than `interval` and it answers
`slow_down`, which means widen your interval and keep it widened.

`authorization_code` exchanges a code from `/oauth/authorize`, with the
`code_verifier` matching the challenge you sent and the same
`redirect_uri`. A code works once: presenting it again also revokes
what the first exchange issued.

`refresh_token` exchanges a refresh token. The presented token is
consumed whatever happens next, so store the new one before using it.
Presenting a consumed refresh token again ends the whole authorization,
since it means the token was copied.

400.description:
An RFC 6749 error. `authorization_pending` and `slow_down` are
normal answers while polling a device authorization, not failures.
`access_denied` means the person refused, and `expired_token` that
the device code is no longer valid: it expired, or it was already
exchanged or refused. `invalid_grant` means the code, device code or
refresh token is not valid for this `client_id`. `invalid_target`
means `resource` names something other than what was authorized.
`slow_down` also answers any grant when this address sends too many
requests.

post.description:
RFC 7009. Always answers 200, even for a token that was never valid, so
it can't be used to test whether a token is live.

Revoking a refresh token ends the whole authorization and takes its
access tokens with it. Revoking an access token affects only that token.

apiKeyQuery.name: apikey
apiKeyQuery.description: `?apikey=<key>`. Convenient in a browser; prefer a header elsewhere.

LookupResponse.description:
The union of every tier's answer. Every answer carries `ip`, `is_bogon`,
`is_vpn`, the Tor and relay members, `is_anycast`, `hostname`, `location` and
`asn`, with or without a key;
each remaining field is present when your tier includes it, and absent
otherwise. A client that must work across plans should treat an absent
flag as unknown rather than as `false`.

ip.description: The address that was looked up, normalized.

is_bogon.description:
Whether the address is reserved space (RFC 1918, loopback, link-local,
documentation ranges and their IPv6 equivalents), answered from the
address alone. Every answer, with or without a key.

is_vpn.description:
Whether the address is VPN infrastructure. Keys off presence in the
VPN dataset, so an unattributed range with no provider is still
`true`.

is_hosting.description: Whether the address belongs to a hosting or cloud provider. Paid plans.

is_relay.description: Whether the address is privacy relay or enterprise web gateway egress, such as iCloud Private Relay or Zscaler. Every answer, with or without a key.

is_tor.description: Whether the address is a Tor node. Every answer, with or without a key.

is_cdn.description: Whether the address belongs to a CDN. Paid plans.

is_resproxy.description: Whether the address was seen in a residential proxy pool. Paid plans.

is_dcproxy.description: Whether the address is one a datacenter proxy service sells or runs on, a proxy company's own ranges included. Paid plans.

is_mobproxy.description: Whether the address was seen in a mobile proxy pool. Paid plans.

is_pubproxy.description: Whether a public proxy, one anyone can connect through, listens on the address or sends its traffic out from it. Paid plans.

is_anycast.description: Whether the address is announced from many places at once, as a public DNS resolver's or a CDN's edge is. Every answer, with or without a key.

is_carrier.description: Whether the address is a mobile carrier's, where many phones can share one address. Paid plans.

is_satellite.description: Whether the address is a satellite operator's. Paid plans.

is_ssh.description: Whether an SSH server answered on the address. Paid plans.

is_smtp.description: Whether a mail server answered on the address. Paid plans.

is_web.description: Whether a web server answered on the address, on port 80 or 443. Paid plans.

is_dns_resolver.description: Whether an open DNS resolver answered on the address. Paid plans.

is_bittorrent.description: Whether a BitTorrent client was seen on the address in the last 90 days. Paid plans.

vpn.description: Detail for `is_vpn`. Empty when `is_vpn` is false. Paid plans.

hosting.description: Detail for `is_hosting`. Empty when false. Paid plans.

relay.description: Detail for `is_relay`. Empty when false. Every answer, with or without a key.

tor.description:
Detail for `is_tor`. Empty when false. Every answer, with or without a
key. The tor dataset carries no provider, so `provider` and
`provider_name` are always empty strings.

cdn.description: Detail for `is_cdn`. Empty when false. Paid plans.

resproxy.description: Detail for `is_resproxy`. Empty when false. Paid plans.

dcproxy.description: Detail for `is_dcproxy`. Empty when false. Paid plans.

mobproxy.description: Detail for `is_mobproxy`. Empty when false. Paid plans.

pubproxy.description: Detail for `is_pubproxy`. Empty when false. Paid plans.

carrier.description: Detail for `is_carrier`. Empty when false. Paid plans.

satellite.description: Detail for `is_satellite`. Empty when false. Paid plans.

ssh.description: Detail for `is_ssh`. Empty when false. Paid plans.

smtp.description: Detail for `is_smtp`. Empty when false. Paid plans.

web.description: Detail for `is_web`: a row per port that answered, lowest first, and `[]` when false. Paid plans.

dns_resolver.description: Detail for `is_dns_resolver`. Empty when false. Paid plans.

bittorrent.description: Detail for `is_bittorrent`. Empty when false. Paid plans.

hostname.description: The name the address's reverse DNS (PTR) record points to, from our IP RDNS database; an empty string when it has none. Every answer, with or without a key.

trial_expired.description:
On every answer to a key on the free plan, and on no other: `false`
while its organization's trial of every field lasts, `true` once the
answer has Unlimited's.

cap_reached.description:
On every answer to a key on a paid plan, and on no other: `false`
while the answer has every field, `true` once its organization's
overage cap is reached and the answer has Unlimited's. Lookups
answered past the cap are not billed; raising or removing the cap in
Billing turns it `false` again.

ips.description:
The addresses to classify, 1 to 1000 per call, counted before
duplicates collapse. Each distinct string is one lookup.

results.description:
One answer per input string that was classified, keyed by the string
as you sent it; the `ip` inside is the normalized form. Each value is
exactly what `GET /{ip}` answers for your plan.

errors.description:
One entry per input string that could not be classified, keyed the
same way. Empty when every entry was answered.

BatchLookupError.description: Why one entry of a batch was not answered, as the single lookup would have reported it.

status.description:
The HTTP status `GET /{ip}` would have answered for this entry: `400`
for a string that is not an address, `500` when the VPN dataset could
not be consulted.

error.description: The same message the single lookup carries for that status.

VpnDetail.description:
What is known about the VPN attribution. Every key is present when the
object is populated, empty values included; the object is `{}` when
`is_vpn` is false.

provider.description: The VPN provider's ID, or an empty string for an unattributed range.

provider_name.description:
The name the provider catalog gives the provider, beside the ID to key on;
an empty string where the catalog names none or the range is unattributed.

last_seen.description: The most recent date this address was observed as VPN infrastructure.

confidence.description: How strongly the attribution is supported.

method.description:
Never returned since 2026-10-20: no plan is answered with the class of
evidence an attribution rests on. Declared so that a client typed
against it keeps compiling; read `confidence` instead.

ClassDetail.description:
The shared detail shape for the hosting, relay, tor and cdn datasets.
Every key is present when the object is populated; the object is `{}`
when its flag is false.

provider.description: The provider's ID, or an empty string where the dataset has none.

provider_name.description:
The name the provider catalog gives the provider; an empty string where the
catalog names none or the dataset has no provider.

confidence.description: How strongly the classification is supported.

last_seen.description: The most recent date this address was observed in this dataset.

ProxyDetail.description:
The shared detail shape for the residential, datacenter and mobile proxy
families, measured over a rolling 90 day window. An address that leaves
the window keeps its flag and the values of its last day in it, so
`last_seen` is what says how recent they are. Every key is present when
the object is populated; the object is `{}` when its flag is false.

provider.description: The proxy network's ID, or an empty string where unattributed.

provider_name.description:
The name the provider catalog gives the proxy network; an empty string where
the catalog names none or the address is unattributed.

first_seen.description:
The earliest date within the window this address was seen in the
pool, as of its last day in the window once it has left.

last_seen.description:
The most recent date this address was seen in the pool. An address
that leaves the window keeps its flag, so this date is what says how
recent the sighting is.

hits.description:
How many times the address was observed in the pool during the
window, as of its last day in it once it has left.

hits_days_pct.description:
The percentage of days in the window on which the address was seen,
as of its last day in it once it has left. A high value means a
stable pool member rather than a one-off sighting.

providers_num.description: How many distinct proxy networks this address was seen in.

PubproxyDetail.description:
The address in Public Proxy IP, open proxies anyone can connect
through, measured over a rolling 90 day window. An address that leaves
the window keeps its flag and the values of its last day in it, so
`last_seen` is what says how recent they are. An address is either
end of a proxy, or both: where it listens, and where its traffic
leaves from. Every key is present when the object is populated; the
object is `{}` when `is_pubproxy` is false.

entry.description: Whether a public proxy listens on this address.

exit.description: Whether a public proxy's traffic leaves from this address.

protocols.description:
The protocols of the proxies listening on or leaving from this
address: `http`, `https` (an HTTP proxy that also tunnels HTTPS),
`socks4` or `socks5`. Empty where only the address is known.

num_ports.description:
How many distinct ports a public proxy listens on at this address;
0 when it is only an exit, or its port is not known.

num_proxies.description:
How many distinct public proxies' traffic left from this address;
0 when it is only an entry.

last_seen.description:
The most recent date a proxy on this address was seen. An address
that leaves the window keeps its flag, so this date is what says how
recent the sighting is.

last_usable.description:
The most recent date within the window a request through a proxy on
this address was answered, as YYYY-MM-DD, or an empty string when
none was, as of its last day in the window once it has left.

Location.description:
Where the address is: the fields of our IP Country database on every
answer, with or without a key, and our IP Geolocation database's finer
ones on a paid plan. Each field your plan includes is present whenever
the object is, so an address in no country, or a private one, answers
empty strings and zeros.

continent.description: Continent code: AF, AN (Antarctica), AS, EU, NA, OC or SA.

currency_code.description: ISO 4217 code of the country's currency, where there is one.

currency_name.description: Name of the country's currency, where there is one.

currency_symbol.description: Symbol of the country's currency, where known.

flag_emoji.description: The country's flag, as an emoji.

flag_unicode.description: The Unicode code points of the flag emoji.

latitude.description: Latitude of the city. Paid plans.

longitude.description: Longitude of the city. Paid plans.

accuracy_radius.description: Radius in km holding the true location with 67% confidence; 20000 for an address announced everywhere, as an anycast one is. Paid plans.

geoname_id.description: GeoNames ID of the city. Paid plans.

dma_code.description: US TV market (DMA) code, empty outside the US. Paid plans.

last_changed.description: The day the range's location last changed. Paid plans.

Asn.description:
The autonomous system that announces the address. Every answer, with or
without a key.
Each field is present whenever the object is: `asn` is 0 and the rest
empty where no announcement covers the address.

asn.description: The AS number, 0 when no announcement covers the address.

name.description: Name of the organization that operates the AS.

domain.description: The AS operator's own registrable domain.

type.description: The kind of network the AS runs: isp, hosting, education, government or business.

prefix.description: The announced BGP prefix that covers the address, the most specific when several do.

country.description: The country the AS's registry assigned it to.

rpki_status.description: The announcement's RPKI status: valid, invalid or not_found.

CarrierDetail.description:
The mobile network whose space the address is, from our Carrier IP
database. Every key is present when the object is populated; the object
is `{}` when `is_carrier` is false.

SatelliteDetail.description:
The satellite operator whose space the address is, from our Satellite IP
database. Every key is present when the object is populated; the object
is `{}` when `is_satellite` is false.

provider.description: The operator's ID in Satellite IP Provider.

segment.description: Who the space serves, such as consumer or maritime.

asn.description: The AS the operator announces it from.

SshDetail.description:
The SSH server that answered on the address, from our SSH IP database.
Every key is present when the object is populated; the object is `{}`
when `is_ssh` is false.

port.description: The port the server answered on.

SmtpDetail.description:
The mail server that answered on the address, from our SMTP IP database.
Every key is present when the object is populated; the object is `{}`
when `is_smtp` is false.

port.description: The port the server answered on.

WebDetail.description: One port of the address that answered as a web server, from our Web IP database.

tls_version.description: The TLS version negotiated, empty without TLS.

first_seen.description: The first day the port was open.

BitTorrentDetail.description:
BitTorrent clients seen on the address over the last 90 days, from our
BitTorrent IP database. Every key is present when the object is
populated; the object is `{}` when `is_bittorrent` is false.

verified.description: A client here answered, or two or more reported it at once.

id_matches_ip.description: A client here derived its node ID from the address (BEP 42).

first_seen.description: The first day a client was seen here.

last_reachable.description: The last day one answered, empty when none did.

indexer.description: A DHT indexer rather than people.

clients.description: The two-letter codes its clients name themselves by.

Company.description:
Who uses the address, from our IP Company database. Paid plans. Every
key is present whenever the object is: empty strings where no record
covers the address.

type.description: What kind of organization: hosting, isp, business, education or government.

AbuseContact.description:
Where to report abuse from the address, from our IP Abuse Contact
database. Paid plans. Every key is present whenever the object is: empty
strings where no record covers the address.

email.description: Where to report abuse from the address.

address.example: Sos. Fabrica de Glucoza, Nr 11B, etaj 1, Sector 2, Bucuresti Romania

network.description: The registry block it was derived from.

validated.description: ARIN reports the contact answered its yearly validation.

LookupError.description: Every non-2xx response carries this shape.

error.description: A human-readable explanation of the failure.

Standing.description:
Where your license for a database family stands today. `licensed` is a
live grant, `expired` one whose term has ended, and `unlicensed` a
database published but never bought.

DatabaseFormat.description: A file format a database version is published in.

bytes.description:
Size of the published file, or null when it has not been published
yet. int64 because it is not hypothetical: resproxy_ip_14d's MMDB is
4.58 GB, so a 32-bit field cannot carry the catalog and `list`
throws for every caller rather than for that one entry.

Database.description:
One database FAMILY, with your organization's license beside it. A license covers
the family, while a download names a specific version, so the IDs you
pass to the download and checksum endpoints come from `versions`.

base.description: The database family, e.g. `vpn_ip`. What the license is held against.

license_type.description:
What a license permits you to do with the data. Null for a family
you hold no license for, which is every one with standing
`unlicensed`.

expires.description: A hard stop. Null when the license has no end date, which is the normal case for a rolling agreement, and when there is no license. A rolling license reports its turnover date in renews_at instead.

renews_at.description: When a rolling license next renews. Null when the license has no defined term, when expires sets a hard stop instead, and when there is no license.

notice_due_at.description: The last day notice of non-renewal can be given for the term ending at renews_at. Null whenever renews_at is, and when the agreement records no notice period.

in_term.description: False when the license has lapsed; downloads are refused.

open.description:
An Open database: free under CC BY-SA 4.0 (credit VPNDetection,
https://vpndetection.io, and share what you build from it under the
same license). Every organization holds a `standard` license to it
from the start, which `standing` and `license_type` report like any
other.

versions.description:
Every published version of this family. The `id` here is what the
download and checksum endpoints take.

id.description: The versioned database ID, e.g. `vpn_ip_v1`. Pass this to download.

sample_formats.description: The formats an evaluation sample is published in, if any.

Download.description:
One download ATTEMPT, refusals included - a denial is what answers "it
stopped working", so they are listed rather than dropped.

sample.description: The evaluation sample rather than the database itself.

open.description: A download of an Open database.

bytes.description:
Object size at redirect time, NOT bytes delivered: the transfer is a
presigned redirect straight to object storage, so we never observe it.
int64 for the same reason as DatabaseFormatSize.bytes - it is the
size of the same object.

apikey_id.description:
The key that made the request. Null when the org acted through the
console rather than through a key.

DbChecksums.description: The published digests for one database file.

update_freq.description: How often a new build is published

entries.description: Row count in the current build

sample.description: A few real rows, keyed by format

sample_size.description: Bytes per format of the evaluation sample, where one is published

sample_entries.description: Row count in the evaluation sample

org_id.description: The organization the key belongs to.

EntitlementApikey.description:
The credential itself. The key is never echoed - only its ID, which is
what the console shows and what you can act on.

expires.description: Null for a key with no end date, which is the normal case.

allowed_cidrs.description:
The source addresses this key may be used from. EMPTY means
unrestricted, never "deny all".

key.description:
The plan the organization is on, as an identifier that is never
renamed or reused: `free` for the free plan, or a paid plan's key.
Compare against it and show `name`. On `free`, usage counts its
trial, the lookups answered with every field.

name.description:
The plan's name, as the site and console show it: `Unlimited` for
the free plan. Show this rather than a name built from `key`: a
plan's name can change, and its key never does.

tier.description:
The field tier, which decides how much of a lookup answer comes
back; `free` is the free plan's. This list never gains a value: a
new plan reports one of these. What each tier includes is documented
on the lookup endpoint rather than repeated here, so there is one
place it can be wrong.

requests.description:
Requests counted in the current window. The same number the lookup
API gates on, and it can lag by a few seconds.

quota.description: What the plan includes. Zero on a plan that includes none.

hard_limit.description:
Where full answers stop: past it, a paid key is answered with
Unlimited's fields and `cap_reached: true`, uncharged, until the
window ends or the cap is raised. NULL means never, which is the
normal state of an uncapped paid plan and is not the same as zero.
Above the quota and below this, requests are served and billed as
overage.

window_start.description: When the current allowance period began.

rc.description: The outcome. `SUCCESS` on success; otherwise the reason.

scopes.description: What this credential may do right now.

ApikeyDetail.description: Key METADATA. Never the key itself.

key_prefix.description: The leading, non-secret part, so a key is recognizable without storing it.

allowed_cidrs.description: Source-IP allowlist. EMPTY MEANS UNRESTRICTED, not deny-all.

retrievable.description: Whether this key's secret can still be read back. False permanently for a key issued before secrets were stored recoverably.

name.description: A label you will recognize later. Shown wherever the key is listed.

allowed_scopes.description: What the new key may do. Omit for a key that carries no named scope, which is the safe default.

key.description: The secret. Returned once, here, and never again.

client_id_metadata_document_supported.description: Any client may sign in with an https `client_id` serving its own metadata.

registration_endpoint.description: RFC 7591 dynamic client registration, for a client that cannot serve its own metadata.

token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported.description: Always `none`. Every client is public and has no secret.

authorization_response_iss_parameter_sup.description: RFC 9207. A redirect back from the authorization endpoint carries `iss`.

scope.description: Space-delimited. Anything your client is not registered for is dropped rather than refused.

resource.description: RFC 8707: what the token is for.

device_code.description: Yours. Poll with it; never show it to anyone.

user_code.description: Short and typable. This is what the person confirms.

verification_uri_complete.description: The same page with the code already filled in.

device_code.description: Required by the device code grant.

code.description: Required by the authorization code grant.

code_verifier.description: Required by the authorization code grant.

redirect_uri.description: Required by the authorization code grant: the `redirect_uri` the code was issued against, exactly.

resource.description: Authorization code grant, optional: RFC 8707, and it must name what was authorized.

refresh_token.description: Required by the refresh token grant.

expires_in.description: Seconds until the access token expires.

refresh_token.description: Always returned. A refresh consumes the token it presents, so keep this one.

scope.description: What was actually granted, which may be narrower than what was asked for.

mslm:apikey_id.description:
Not part of OAuth, and only for our own clients. The ID of the API
key the person picked when they approved, returned by every grant
while this authorization may still read that key back. Absent when
no key was picked, or when the person's role no longer allows
reading keys back.

mslm:apikey.description:
Not part of OAuth, and only for our own clients: a client that signed
in with a Client ID Metadata Document or registered itself never
receives a key. The API
key itself, so a device ends up holding an ordinary key. Returned by
the device code and authorization code grants only, never by a
refresh, and only alongside
`mslm:apikey_id`. Absent when that key's secret cannot be read back,
which is the case for a key created before keys could be shown again
in the console; a rotated key can be.

redirect_uris.description: One to ten, each matched exactly, apart from a loopback one's port.

client_name.description: Shown to the person as your client's own claim, marked unverified, beside where its redirect goes.

client_id_issued_at.description: Unix seconds. 64-bit, since 32 bits run out on 2038-01-19.

client_name.description: As the person will see it.

scope.description: The most this client may be granted: `apikeys.use`.

token.description: An access token or a refresh token.

Unauthorized.description: Missing or invalid key, or the key lacks the db.download scope

KeyOverHttp.description: The key was sent over plain HTTP (`KEY_OVER_HTTP`), refused whatever it is. By then it has crossed in the clear, so use `https://` and replace a key that did

NotAvailable.description: Today's copy has not been published yet

AccountUnauthorized.description: No credential was presented, or it is not valid.

AccountForbidden.description:
The credential does not hold the scope this endpoint requires
(`FORBIDDEN`); the missing scope is deliberately not named. Or the
credential was sent over plain HTTP, refused whatever it is
(`KEY_OVER_HTTP`): use `https://`.
`rc`: `FORBIDDEN`, `KEY_OVER_HTTP`.

AccountNotFound.description: No such key in this organization.

AccountInvalid.description: The request body is missing a required field.

ApikeyIdParam.name: id
ApikeyIdParam.description: The key's ID, as returned by the list endpoint. Never the key itself.
